summary.text: David Brock Smith is the Republican nominee and a sitting Oregon state senator from Port Orford. A small-business owner who took over his family's restaurant, he held local office, served on the Curry County Board of Commissioners, and was elected to the Oregon House in 2016 before moving to the state Senate in 2023. His campaign says he is running to bring a rural voice to Washington.

paragraphs.text: Born in Port Orford, Oregon, in 1976 or 1977. He is a third-generation Southwest Oregon resident, according to his campaign website.
Earned an associate degree from Southwestern Oregon Community College and a bachelor's degree from Southern Oregon University.
Worked in the culinary industry in the Rogue Valley, then took over his family's Port Orford restaurant, the Port & Starboard, from his parents, according to his campaign website.
Served on the Port Orford City Council (including as president), the school board, the Curry County Planning Commission, and as president of the North Curry County Chamber of Commerce.
Elected to the Curry County Board of Commissioners in 2012.
Elected to the Oregon House of Representatives in 2016 (District 1) and served from January 2017 to January 2023.

Appointed to the Oregon State Senate for District 1 in January 2023, succeeding Dallas Heard, and elected to a full term in 2024. In the 2021-2022 session he was vice chair of the House Energy and Environment Committee.
Won the Republican primary for U.S. Senate on May 19, 2026.
